# resolving-merge-conflicts

`/resolving-merge-conflicts` — a model-invoked engineering skill for resolving an **in-progress git merge/rebase conflict**. It reads the current merge/rebase state, finds the **primary sources** for each conflicting change (commit messages, PRs, original issues) to understand each side's intent, then resolves every hunk — preserving both intents where possible, or picking the one matching the merge's stated goal and noting the trade-off (never inventing new behaviour, never `--abort`). It runs the project's automated checks (typecheck → tests → format), fixes anything the merge broke, and finishes the merge/rebase with a commit.

**New in v1.1 (2026-07-09).** An integration-time implementation skill: understanding change intent from primary sources ([[pattern-source-grounding]]) to keep a shared trunk mergeable ([[pattern-trunk-based-development]]). No cross-framework counterpart — the other frameworks handle integration inside their ship/execute steps rather than as a dedicated conflict-resolution skill.

# wayfinder

`/wayfinder` — a user-invoked engineering skill for planning **a huge chunk of work — more than one agent session can hold** — as a **shared map of investigation tickets** on the repo's issue tracker, resolved one at a time until the way to the **destination** is clear. Naming the destination is the first act; the map (a single `wayfinder:map` issue whose child issues are its tickets) is an *index*, not a store — it gists each closed decision and links to the ticket that holds it. **Plan, don't do**: tickets resolve *decisions*, not deliverables; the pull to just build is the signal you've reached the map's edge and should hand off (to [[mp-to-spec]] / [[mp-to-tickets]] / [[mp-implement]]).

**New in v1.1 (2026-07-09)** — graduated from `in-progress/` (was `decision-mapping`) into `engineering/`. Positioned as a **situational on-ramp** (greenfield project or a feature too big for one session), *not* the default entry flow — the grill-led `idea → ship` chain stays the front door. Every ticket is classified **HITL** (human-in-the-loop: grilling, prototype) or **AFK** (agent-alone: research; `task` either), and blocking prefers the tracker's native dependency links so the frontier renders in the tracker UI. It sizes ceremony to work bigger than a single context ([[pattern-scale-adaptive-planning]]) and advances one fresh session at a time ([[pattern-fresh-context-subagents]]). No cross-framework counterpart — the investigation-map-for- oversized-work framing is unique to MP.

## See Also
- [[mp-to-tickets]] — the sibling for work that *does* fit a normal decomposition; wayfinder feeds into it once the fog clears.
- [[mp-grill-with-docs]] · [[mp-grill-me]] — the front-door grill skills that signpost *up* to wayfinder when an effort is too big to hold.
- [[bmad-sprint-planning]] — BMAD's large-work backlog mapping (a loose relative).
- [[stage-align]] — the canonical stage this implements (it resolves *decisions* about what to build, upstream of the spec; [[mp-to-spec]] then writes the spec in [[stage-specify]]).

`/ask-matt` — a user-invoked **router** over the skills in the repo: "you don't remember every skill, so ask." It describes **flows** (paths through the skills) anchored on one **main flow**, two **on-ramps**, a codebase-health lane, a **vocabulary layer** underneath, and a list of standalone skills.

## The main flow (v1.3.1)

1. [[mp-grill-with-docs]] sharpens the idea in a working directory. With no working directory, use [[mp-grill-me]].
2. *Branch:* if a question needs a runnable answer, detour through [[mp-prototype]], bridged out and back by [[mp-handoff]].
3. *Branch:* is this a multi-session build?
   - **Yes** → [[mp-to-spec]] → [[mp-to-tickets]], then either [[mp-implement]] per ticket (`/clear` between each) **or** [[mp-implement-spec]] for the whole spec at once (implementer subagents across the ready frontier, one integration branch).
   - **No** → [[mp-implement]] in the same context.
   - Either way the build drives [[mp-tdd]] and closes with [[mp-code-review]]. When the work goes up as a PR, [[mp-pr]] shapes the body.
4. [[mp-retro]] **closes the loop**: it suggests changes to the agent's *environment* (checks, standards, pointers, tooling) so the next build starts better.

**On-ramps:** [[mp-triage]] (raw incoming issues only; tickets from `/to-tickets` are already agent-ready, so "don't triage them"), [[mp-diagnosing-bugs]] (then `/retro` once the fix is in; v1.3.1), and [[mp-wayfinder]] (the "most cognitively demanding flow", reserved for an idea that won't fit one session). When wayfinder's map clears, "it hands off, it doesn't build": merge onto the main flow at [[mp-to-spec]], not straight into `/implement`.

**Standalone:** [[mp-grill-me]], [[mp-grilling]], [[mp-prototype]], [[mp-research]], [[mp-to-questionnaire]], [[mp-wizard]], [[mp-wait-what]], `teach`, [[mp-writing-for-agents]]. **Codebase health:** [[mp-improve-codebase-architecture]]. **Vocabulary underneath:** [[mp-domain-modeling]], [[mp-codebase-design]].

A **phase** is a chunk of work inside a session (the grilling, the implementation, the QA). At the boundary between two phases there are five options, in order:

- **`/clear`**: when nothing here matters to what's next.
- **[[mp-handoff]]**: narrowed in v1.2.0. It is only for when something must *travel*: a new harness, a new directory, a colleague, or a side task forked mid-phase.
- **Subagent**: a tightly scoped task run AFK in its own window.
- **`/compact`**: the default, at the bottom of the tree rather than the first reach.

# resolving-merge-conflicts

> **Removed in v1.3.0 (2026-10-04).** "It's no longer needed, and nothing replaces it: the agent works through an in-progress merge or rebase conflict without a dedicated skill." It left the Claude Code plugin, the README, and the [[mp-ask-matt]] router; its docs page stays up, marked archived. This page is kept as a historical record so existing links still resolve. Its `implements:` edge is retained for the record, and [[stage-implement]] lists it as removed.

`/resolving-merge-conflicts` was a model-invoked engineering skill for resolving an **in-progress git merge/rebase conflict**. It read the current merge/rebase state and found the **primary sources** for each conflicting change (commit messages, PRs, original issues) to understand each side's intent. It then resolved every hunk, preserving both intents where possible or picking the one that matched the merge's stated goal and noting the trade-off. It never invented new behaviour and never ran `--abort`. Finally it ran the project's automated checks (typecheck → tests → format), fixed anything the merge broke, and finished the merge/rebase with a commit.

**Added in v1.1 (2026-07-09).** It was an integration-time implementation skill: understanding change intent from primary sources ([[pattern-source-grounding]]) to keep a shared trunk mergeable ([[pattern-trunk-based-development]]). It had no cross-framework counterpart. The retirement itself is evidence: integration conflict handling was judged to be default agent competence, not a discipline worth a skill. In v1.3.0 its nearest successor in spirit is [[mp-implement-spec]], which avoids most conflicts by design (each implementer merges the integration tip into its own branch first, so every merge is a fast-forward).

# prototype

`/prototype` — a **model-invoked** (since v1.1; it was user-invoked before) engineering skill that builds a **throwaway prototype** to answer one design question: does this state model feel right, or what should this UI look like ([[pattern-throwaway-prototype]]). Being model-invoked, the agent and other skills can reach for it autonomously. In MP's main flow it is the prototype detour, bridged into and out of by [[mp-handoff]] when a question needs a runnable answer.

## v1.2.0 reshape (2026-08-05): one HTML file, kept as a primary source

The changelog builds it on two ideas:

- **The demo is a single shareable HTML file.** The logic branch no longer builds a terminal app. It produces one self-contained file (plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build, no server) that a non-developer can open by double-click and drive in their own domain language. The file has a labelled state panel, always-available free-play buttons, and tabbed **guided walkthroughs** (each a scenario with the ordered buttons to press). The portable pure-logic module still lifts into the real code; the HTML shell is the throwaway. The UI branch still produces radically different variations toggleable from one route.
- **The prototype is a primary source.** "Throwaway is a constraint on how the code is written, not a promise to destroy it." The prototype is no longer deleted once it has answered its question. It is captured as runnable evidence on a throwaway **`prototype/<name>` branch** out of main, with a context pointer on the implementation issue. Main keeps only the validated decision, and the exploration stays findable. The verdict and the question are still recorded durably in an issue, ADR, or commit.

The second idea shifts the [[pattern-throwaway-prototype]] pattern from *build → learn → discard* to *build → learn → archive off-trunk*. [[mp-wayfinder]] uses the same move for research (`research/<name>` branches).

# wayfinder

`/wayfinder` — a user-invoked engineering skill for planning **a huge chunk of work — more than one agent session can hold** — as a **shared map of investigation tickets** on the repo's issue tracker, resolved one at a time until the way to the **destination** is clear. Naming the destination is the first act; the map (a single `wayfinder:map` issue whose child issues are its tickets) is an *index*, not a store — it gists each closed decision and links to the ticket that holds it. **Plan, don't do**: tickets resolve *decisions*, not deliverables; the pull to just build is the signal you've reached the map's edge and should hand off (to [[mp-to-spec]] / [[mp-to-tickets]] / [[mp-implement]]).

**New in v1.1 (2026-07-09)** — graduated from `in-progress/` (was `decision-mapping`) into `engineering/`. Positioned as a **situational on-ramp** (greenfield project or a feature too big for one session), *not* the default entry flow — the grill-led `idea → ship` chain stays the front door. Every ticket is classified **HITL** (human-in-the-loop: grilling, prototype) or **AFK** (agent-alone: research; `task` either), and blocking prefers the tracker's native dependency links so the frontier renders in the tracker UI. It sizes ceremony to work bigger than a single context ([[pattern-scale-adaptive-planning]]) and advances one fresh session at a time ([[pattern-fresh-context-subagents]]). No cross-framework counterpart — the investigation-map-for- oversized-work framing is unique to MP.

# grilling

A **model-invoked** productivity skill: the reusable interview loop that underlies both [[mp-grill-me]] and [[mp-grill-with-docs]]. It is the canonical implementation of [[pattern-grilling]] — keep asking until decision branches resolve — factored out so other skills compose it rather than re-implement it.

A **model-invoked** engineering skill that actively builds and sharpens the project's domain model — challenging terms against the glossary, stress-testing with edge-case scenarios, and updating the `CONTEXT.md` shared-language glossary ([[artifact-domain-model]]) and ADRs ([[artifact-adr]]) inline. **New in v1.1 (2026-07-09).** This is the first time Matt Pocock's toolkit has a first-class *execute* skill — previously "building" was only the test-first [[mp-tdd]] and throwaway [[mp-prototype]]. `implement` makes MP a full member of the cross-framework **execute** cluster: walk the plan/tickets unit-by-unit, test-driven — alongside [[gsd-execute-phase]], [[openspec-apply]], [[speckit-implement]], [[addy-incremental-implementation]], [[bmad-dev-story]], and [[ce-work]]. It is the tail of MP's main flow: `idea → grill → to-spec → to-tickets → implement (per ticket, fresh context) → code-review`.

+> **v1.3.0 (2026-10-04): a parallel sibling.** [[mp-implement-spec]] now offers the whole-spec alternative: implementer subagents across the ready frontier, landing on one integration branch, with one [[mp-code-review]] at the end. `/implement` stays the per-ticket path (one ticket per fresh context, tdd + code-review each time), and the in-place path for work too small for a spec. When the work goes up as a PR, [[mp-pr]] shapes the body; [[mp-retro]] follows as the main flow's last step.
- [[mp-to-tickets]] — produces the tickets this builds (one per fresh context window).
- [[mp-tdd]] — the red-green engine this drives at seams.
- [[pattern-deterministic-gates]] — the continuous typecheck/test discipline it runs while building.

MP's member of the cross-framework **decompose** cluster: it slices work into dependency-ordered, independently-shippable units, like [[addy-planning]], [[speckit-tasks]], and BMAD's [[bmad-create-epics-and-stories]]; [[speckit-taskstoissues]] is the export half Spec Kit splits into a second command. +> **v1.2.0 (2026-08-05): one file per ticket locally.** On the local-markdown tracker, tickets are now one file each under `.scratch/<feature>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md` (never a combined `tickets.md`), and the spec file is `spec.md`, not `PRD.md`. Its blocking edges are what [[mp-implement-spec]] (v1.3.0) reads as a **task graph** to schedule parallel implementers off the ready frontier.

- [[seeds-plan-submit]] — the same decomposition run by a program: an AJV-validated plan whose steps spawn the tickets and whose `blocks` indices become real dependency edges, into a JSONL store in the repo rather than a hosted tracker.
- [[mp-wayfinder]] — the sibling for work too big to decompose in one session (investigation-ticket map).

# Matt Pocock — Skills for Real Engineers

A curated set of small, composable agent skills by **Matt Pocock** "for real engineering work — not 'vibe coding'", sourced from his personal `.claude` directory and designed to be adapted ("Hack around with them. Make them your own."). Works with any model and any coding agent. Explicitly positioned *against* owning-the-process frameworks: "Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve." These skills stay small and composable instead.

+- **Install (v1.2.0+):** two paths, "two philosophies". The **Claude Code plugin** (`claude plugins install mattpocock-skills`, in the official marketplace) is a managed, read-only bundle that self-updates: "you subscribe rather than fork". **`npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`** (skills.sh) copies editable files for Codex and other agents. "Pick one: installing both leaves you with every skill twice."
- **Configure:** `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` (issue tracker — GitHub/Linear/local files, triage labels, doc paths).

+**Dual-harness since v1.2.0.** Every skill ships an `agents/openai.yaml` beside its `SKILL.md` with Codex UI metadata, and user-invoked skills set `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` (the Codex analog of `disable-model-invocation: true`). `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`. A native Codex plugin is deferred (ADR 0002). `runs_on:` stays `[[claude-code]]` only, since the wiki has no Codex harness page (support-scope rule).

Unlike [[gsd]] — a single end-to-end workflow engine — this is a **loose toolkit of independent skills**, each **user-invoked** (typed as a slash command; orchestrates) or **model-invoked** (typed *or* auto-reached-for by the agent; holds reusable discipline). A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked ones, never another user-invoked one.
